q-181958:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

To create a schematic of the Cartesian product, we create a table and list the elements of the first set $A$ in a row across the top and the elements of the second set $B$ in a column down the left side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/6baae52e45d00d31eac732a23be655b648765c27cfcdc667c511b176d5bbbc88.png)

Then, at each intersection, we write an ordered pair whose first coordinate is the corresponding element of $A$ and the second coordinate is the corresponding element of $B.$

Our completed $A\times B$ schematic is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/38e9d12b0c09ae066149d95235a6918712214edc147c57775da2d880b584cb9e.png)

q-105862:
For any two finite sets $A$ and $B,$ the cardinality of $A\times B$ is

$$
|A\times B|=|A|\cdot |B|.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|M\times M| & =|M|\cdot |M| \\  & =10\cdot 10 \\  & =100.\end{aligned}
$$

q-105861:
For any two finite sets $M$ and $N,$ the cardinality of $M\times N$ is

$$
|M\times N|=|M|\cdot |N|.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|M\times N| & =|M|\cdot |N| \\  & =7\cdot 6 \\  & =42.\end{aligned}
$$
